Flat uniform neutral medium grey background, no gradient, no text, labels, logos, ground lines or effects. Flat even lighting; precise clean cel shading with just 2–3 tones per material and dark colored seams between armor plates. Crisp game-production model-sheet illustration with enough detail to make the mechanisms legible, not a photorealistic render.

Preserve the current design faithfully: a wide low knuckle-walking gorilla with extremely long bulky green armored arms and huge orange boxy fists, small bent green rear legs and orange toes. Pine/moss green segmented angular armor, orange split chest panels, grey mechanical connectors and pistons, dark hubs with steel rims, green ridged angular helmet, narrow flat cyan visor and grey lower jaw. Fists have large circular side hubs and grey/dark knuckle mechanisms, with orange armored digits. Follow the attached current shape and hardware placement exactly in each view. Three grey ballast blocks with orange caps across the upper back in the arrangement shown in the attachment. Asymmetric shoulder weapons: one cylindrical gatling/cannon and one box launcher pod; preserve the reference's anatomical sides, do not mirror or duplicate them. Follow the reference back armor and leg geometry, including segmented haunch/calf plates, exposed steel connectors and orange toes. Retain small vents and mechanical inset details only where the reference supports them. No fur, skin, tail, extra limbs, added horns, invented weapons, glowing aura or bloom. Cyan visor is a flat colored surface. Do not import a different gorilla design or exaggerate it into a new machine.

Render the fine reference details through intelligent pixel simplification while maintaining the exact recognizable machine. The cyan visor is a crisp colored strip without light spill.
prompts.wolf_20261019_model_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: orthographic mechanical-creature model sheet, four views of one identical design.
Input image: the attached sprite sheet is the sole design reference. It shows our original heavy quadrupedal WOLF machine. Ignore all earlier creatures and wolf variants in the conversation.
Primary request: translate THIS EXACT machine into a clean, detailed orthographic model sheet, preserving its silhouette, proportions, part counts, armor layout and colors. Not a redesign.
Composition: four full-body views in a spacious 2-by-2 layout: upper left true side facing right, upper right true front, lower left true back, lower right front three-quarter facing right. Same physical scale in every panel, consistent height and common standing pose. Orthographic projection throughout, including the three-quarter axonometric view: no perspective convergence, no oversized near limbs. Each machine entirely visible with generous margins; tails and fins must fit.
Design invariants from the reference: broad dark graphite torso and layered spine armor; distinctly heavy rounded forearm armor and forepaws, narrower bent digitigrade hind legs; off-white face cheeks, shoulder caps, angular outer hip plates and shin insets; short wedge-shaped canine muzzle with small pale fangs and cyan eye lenses; gold armored brow ridge, small gold joints and gold toe/claw caps; exactly two short upright wolf ears, white edges and red inner strips, paired close together at the back of the head; exactly two long thin tapered dark dorsal fins/blades, mounted one on each side behind the head, swept upward and backward with gold edges and pale tips, matching the supplied front/back views; long articulated tapered grey armored tail with a solid red tip; pale overlapping diagonal flank/rib plates. Preserve the reference's small colored chest hardware. Keep left/right placement consistent across all views. Do not invent guns, spikes, panels, antennae or decorative markings.
Rendering: crisp clean cel-shaded model-sheet illustration, precise dark seam lines between armor plates, 2–3 discrete tones per material, flat even neutral lighting. Flat neutral medium-grey background matching the source mood; no cast shadows, glow, bloom, painterly texture, scratches, typography, labels, letters, numbers, logos, panel borders or watermarks. This first deliverable is the four-view clean model sheet, not the pixel-art battle sprite.
prompts.wolf_20261019_model_refine_prompt:

Keep the exact grey/off-white/gold/red/cyan wolf machine design, its heavy forelegs, bent hind legs, overlapping rib plates, long red-tipped segmented tail, TWO paired ears and TWO swept dorsal blade fins. Refine the model sheet into a proper orthographic turnaround with these targeted corrections:

Show the near side in exact profile, no front face of the chest or nose and no three-quarter body turning; far limbs may be visible only through their standing-pose stagger. Keep the exact reference proportions.
2. Upper right is a true front elevation. Lower left is a true back elevation. Lower right is an orthographic front three-quarter at 45 degrees facing right.
3. Identical physical scale and proportions in all four panels. Align the feet within each row, align shoulder and head heights between corresponding front and back elevations, same leg lengths, no enlarged back view. Complete creature with tail and blade fins fully contained and breathing room.
4. Completely FLAT uniform neutral grey background, no gradient or vignette, no shadows. Flat even lighting, two or three crisp cel-shaded tones per material. Thin dark local-color seams between armor plates.
Keep every other aspect of the original design; no extra spikes, guns, antennas or redesigned parts. No text, labels, logos, panel borders or watermark.
